name: SwiftPM prebuilt swift-syntax for macros
baseline: Building swift-syntax from source for every package that uses macros (SwiftPM and Xcode before the prebuilts)
verdict_reason: Apple says prebuilt swift-syntax cuts clean builds 'by minutes' for some projects, and independent users report 180 s to 120 s clean builds, nearly 3 minutes saved on Linux, and a macro build penalty down from 40 s to 16 s. The gain applies only to macro-using projects on swift-syntax versions with published prebuilts.
tier_reason: Numbers come from developers outside the SwiftPM team on the Swift Forums, but each is a single anecdotal report without a reproducible setup.
claimed_speedup: Clean build from around 180s to 120s (33%) on an M4 Pro MacBook Pro; nearly 3 minutes saved on a simple Linux build; macro incremental penalty from 40s to 16s; Apple: clean builds shorter 'by minutes' for some projects
workload: Clean and incremental builds of apps and packages that depend on macro packages built on swift-syntax
hardware: M4 Pro MacBook Pro (one report); Linux (one report)
toolchain: Swift 6.1.1 with --enable-experimental-prebuilts, Xcode 16.4 with IDEPackageEnablePrebuilts; Swift 6.2 / Xcode 26
install: built into Swift 6.2 toolchains and Xcode 26 (opt-in preview in Swift 6.1.1 and Xcode 16.4)
one_liner: SwiftPM downloads a release-built swift-syntax for macros instead of compiling it, cutting minutes from clean builds.
how_it_is_fast: Macro implementations depend on swift-syntax, a large Swift library that every clean build had to compile, which is slow in release mode and on small CI machines. SwiftPM now downloads a prebuilt binary matching the resolved swift-syntax version, the host platform and the compiler version, and falls back to building from source when none exists. The prebuilts are release builds, so macros can also run faster.
use_it_when: Projects that depend on macro packages (swift-syntax based) and do frequent clean or CI builds
Release-configuration builds, where compiling swift-syntax is slowest
skip_it_when: swift-syntax versions or toolchains with no published prebuilt: SwiftPM builds from source as before
Setups that hit SDK-mismatch errors with the prebuilt modules, as several preview users did
caveats: All numbers are single forum reports without project details or repeated runs
Apple's own claim ('by minutes') is directional
Early previews had SDK-version mismatch errors and missing prebuilts for some toolchain versions
tradeoffs: Downloads binaries from download.swift.org during resolution
Prebuilts exist only for specific swift-syntax releases, and the URL pattern is not a stable API

evidence.quote: To speed up your build, the latest releases of Swift PM and Xcode support pre-built swift-syntax dependencies. This completely eliminates an expensive build step, and for some projects, it reduces clean build times by minutes.
On an M4 Pro MBP a clean build has gone down from around 180s to 120s, a 33% improvement!
Saves nearly 3 minutes for a simple build on Linux!
Looks like this knocks our incremental build penalty from 40s to 16s in the Emit Swift Module phase
